working_title: March 2025 Flood Event: Hydrometeorological Trigger and Observed Road Disruption
scientific_question: Did the March 2025 event contain sufficiently strong and spatially coherent rainfall to support the documented road-disruption episode?
panels: A) 19–21 Mar JB area-weighted rainfall timeline; B) 1 h/3 h/6 h peaks + Senai gauge comparison; C) observed JKR closure sections over flood-evidence/hotspot context
frozen_key_results: JB 72 h area-weighted rainfall 271.33 mm; 20 Mar 156.47 mm; local 6 h peak 97.51 mm; Senai gauge 176.2 mm/day vs IMERG 143.23 mm/day; 3 primary Mar-20 closure sections
main_claim: The primary accessibility event was embedded in a strong rainfall episode with spatially matched documented road disruption.
do_not_claim: IMERG is perfectly calibrated; rainfall directly caused every closure at an exact hour.

working_title: Observed Flood Closures Produce Localized Healthcare-Network Disconnection
scientific_question: How much did the documented March-20 road closures change healthcare accessibility, and where was the effect concentrated?
panels: A) baseline vs disrupted accessibility map; B) newly unreachable population + 30/45/60 min coverage change; C) subdistrict concentration (Tebrau vs Plentong)
frozen_key_results: Nominal newly unreachable 4961; 30-min coverage change -0.260 pp; citywide mean delay only 0.009 min; Tebrau dominant
main_claim: The event did not create a large citywide mean delay; it created a spatially concentrated loss of network reachability.
do_not_claim: Large citywide travel-time deterioration; p-value significance from 75,149 spatial cells.

working_title: Closure-Location Sensitivity and Robustness of the Accessibility-Loss Pattern
scientific_question: Are the main accessibility-loss conclusions robust to uncertainty in closure position?
panels: A) 27-scenario distribution of newly unreachable population; B) Tebrau share range; C) single-road sensitivity for J105, FT01, FT003
frozen_key_results: Newly unreachable range 2554–5079; Tebrau share 85.4–94.4%; J105 location-sensitive; FT01 stable
main_claim: The qualitative finding of localized healthcare-network disconnection, dominated by Tebrau, is robust to declared closure-location uncertainty.
do_not_claim: Exactly 4,961 people under all plausible closure locations; J105 uniquely ranks first in every sensitivity case.

working_title: Flood Susceptibility × Healthcare Criticality Reveals Preparedness Priorities
scientific_question: Which flood-susceptible roads also carry high healthcare-network dependency, and which corridors should be prioritized before future events?
panels: A) CRPI map; B) flood susceptibility × healthcare criticality matrix; C) top named non-observed preparedness corridors
frozen_key_results: 1,458 eligible susceptible+dependent core segments; 74 P1; 218 P2; CRPI rank robustness Spearman 0.991–0.999; top-100 overlap 99/101
main_claim: Preparedness priorities can be identified by combining evidence-based flood susceptibility with healthcare-network criticality.
do_not_claim: CRPI is flood probability, expected annual loss, or a direct predictor of people made unreachable.

working_title: Recovery Sequencing Reduces Spatial Inequality in Healthcare Accessibility
scientific_question: Which recovery sequence restores the most healthcare access, and does it preferentially reduce the spatially concentrated Tebrau disadvantage?
panels: A) all 6 recovery orders; B) cumulative restored population for nominal best order; C) Tebrau/Plentong restoration by stage; D) equity Gini trajectory / recovery-stage origin map
frozen_key_results: Nominal J105-first restores 3220 (64.9%); J105+FT01 restore 4499 (90.7%); robust Tier 1 = J105+FT01, Tier 2 = FT003
main_claim: Most modeled healthcare-isolation loss can be removed by restoring J105 and FT01 first, with the dominant equity benefit accruing to Tebrau.
do_not_claim: J105 must always be first under all spatial uncertainty.
